To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the levels of IL 1, IL 6, IL 8 and TNF α were elevated in patients with AA; (2) the level of IL 1 in bone marrow was related to the severity of the disease; and (3) the levels of these inflammatory cytokines decreased after successful treatment.
the abnormal T cell activation and its related immunologically active cytokines are involved in the pathogenesis and prognosis of aplastic anemias.

an abnormally increased autoreactive T lymphocyte activity, combined with several immunologically active molecules, which are cytotoxic for hematopoeitic stem cells, is a major cause of haematopoietic failure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunologic mechanism of AA and the role of immunosuppressive therapy in its treatment.
the mechanism of AA and the relationship between the immune response and clinical outcome.
the pathogenetic mechanisms of AA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pathogenesis of AA is multifactorial and that the immune system plays a major role.
the immune system is malfunctioned in patients with AA, and that it is a complex, multi-faceted, and multi-factor process.

the pathogenesis of AA is a complex process, which involves the interaction of many factors, including genetic factors, environmental factors, and the interaction between immune and hemopoietic systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a T lymphocyte-mediated immune destruction of hematopoietic cells is the main cause of AA.
the pathogenesis of AA is a T cell-mediated autoimmune process.
a T lymphocyte mediated autoimmune reaction is a major cause of AA, and the level of sFasL, IL 2 and IL 2R are good markers for the clinical outcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the abnormal immune response of the patients is the major factor in the pathogenesis, and the abnormal immune response is related to the clinical prognosis.
it is important for the treatment of AA to control these immunological abnormalities and the level of these cytokines may be a good indicator of the efficacy of treatment.
we need to focus on the role of the immune system in the development of AA and the role of cytokines in the regulation of immune function in AA.
